mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS > 2.0% periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher labor market disengagement typically precedes equity market pullbacks.
regime_hint: rising unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of UNRATE > 5% months.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% for two consecutive quarters, it signals robust demand, leading to a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during qualifying GDPC1-INDPRO gaps.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as investors anticipate price reallocation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a month and FEDFUNDS remains below 1%, it signals inflation concern without aggressive policy, predicting a negative S&P 20-day return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during such inflation-policing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly PAYEMS increase exceeding 100,000 jobs when UNRATE is below 4% signals labor market strengthening and supports a positive S&P 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) during such labor expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in HOUST (household spending) of over 2% while RSAFS (retail sales) remains flat is a contrarian signal predicting a positive S&P 20-day return as demand softens selectively.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month decrease > 2% and RSAFS flat
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months and INDPRO is rising, it indicates a supply-side improvement that is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for two consecutive months and INDPRO rising
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) during qualifying UNRATE/INDPRO regimes.
